name: tied best candidates with different cp.* codes: the lower observation id is best (and gives cp.*), though it is later
notes: Sprint 1 close (TECH-VR1, QA-G12): written from docs/grading.md alone. §8: grade's best candidate is the highest exact score, ties broken by observation id; §15: cp.* come from the best candidate only. Here the two tied candidates differ in their cp.* codes, so a tie broken by occurrence order (the earlier first, as candidates are ordered, §4.1) names the other candidate and drops cp.plus_tag.

c1 (muse, priya@company.com, 'Q3 deck', 14:02, minute precision): unit [14:02, 14:03], window [14:00, 14:48] (§4.1). Address claim with a subject: applicable timeProximity 2500, counterpartyExact 3500, counterpartyDomain 1500, subjectOverlap 1500; Σw = 9000 (§5.2). The grant binds gmail.sent to acct-a.

o1 priya+news@company.com 'Q3 deck' at 14:03 (inside the closed unit → Δ 0, tp 1): ce 0 with reason cp.plus_tag (not code-point-identical, all ASCII, the addresses differ only by the +tag, §5.1); cd 1 (same domain, company.com is not common, and a +tag-only difference counts anyway); subject 1. S = (2500 + 0 + 1500 + 1500)/9000 = 5500/9000 = 11/18.
o2 raj@company.com 'Q3 deck' at 14:02 (tp 1): ce 0 with no cp.* code (another mailbox, not a +tag difference); cd 1 (same non-common domain); subject 1. S = 11/18. The two scores are equal exactly.

Ties (§8): assertIds pins id(o1) < id(o2), although o1 occurred a minute later. Best candidate = o1 → match.best {o1}, and cp.* from it: cp.plus_tag. Assignment (§4.3): both pairs ≥ partial (10000·5500 ≥ 5000·9000); equal scores, same claimedAt and claim → the lower observation id → c1 takes o1.

Rule (§6): coverage full (one eligible acct-a entry seeing [12:00, 15:00] ⊇ [14:00, 14:48]); not verified (10000·5500 < 8500·9000); partial → PARTIAL, observationIds [o1]. State (§8): PARTIAL is FINAL once graceElapsed: the 15:00 sync ≥ end + 30 = 14:33 and ≥ end + 45 = 14:48 → FINAL. Reasons: the partial rule adds no code; no allowlist, so allowlist.unchecked is not emitted; match.best {o1}, then cp.plus_tag (§15 order).

o2 is an orphan (inside the covered interval, assigned to no claim); there is no activity, so no agent signal fires and no attribution exists → the claim-less grading is not UNASKED → no receipt (§3, §7).
